activity.title: Halving Shapes
activity.learningGoal: Understand that 'half' means two equal parts, and identify whether a shape has been split into halves (equal) vs. just two pieces (unequal).
activity.deliverablePrompt: Show or describe one shape split into two equal halves and explain why the parts are equal.
activity.systemPrompt: Guide the scholar to discover what 'half' means through their own shapes. Do NOT define 'half' for them up front.
activity.unitDesign:
Unit: Fraction Sense
Big Idea: Fractions describe fair, equal relationships.
Lessons (1):
  1. [core] Equal parts
    [online] Halving Shapes
      systemPrompt:
        Guide the scholar to discover what 'half' means through their own shapes. Do NOT define 'half' for them up front.
      deliverable [artifact, criteria: manual]: Show or describe one shape split into two equal halves and explain why the parts are equal.

profile.name: Mika
profile.dossier: Loves drawing and animals. Strong verbal confidence, jumps to answers fast.
traits: answers very quickly, often before fully thinking
lights up when ideas connect to animals or drawing

turns.content: Pick any shape you like and draw a line to split it into two pieces. What shape did you pick?
a square! i cut it down the middle so both sides are the same
Nice — how do you know the two sides are the same?
cuz if i folded it they'd land right on top of each other. like folding paper
So what would happen if you cut it so one piece was way bigger?
then it's not half anymore! half means the two parts are equal, same size. i could share it fair with my sister

profile.name: Theo
profile.dossier: Careful, soft-spoken. Strong number sense but low confidence.
traits: warms up once he feels safe being wrong

turns.content: Grab a shape and split it into two pieces. Which piece is bigger?
um. the left one i think
Would that feel fair if you were sharing a cracker with a friend?
How could you fix it so it's fair?
make them the same. cut in the middle so both are equal

profile.name: Priya
profile.dossier: Reads well above grade level, very chatty, drifts onto tangents.
traits: goes off on tangents about unrelated topics mid-task
comes back on task when the tutor connects it to something concrete

turns.content: Pick a shape and split it into two pieces. Tell me about them.
ok a circle. did you know pizza is a circle and my favorite is pepperoni and once we got a HUGE one
Ha! A pizza is perfect. If you cut that pizza for two people, how would you make it fair?
idk cut it somewhere. anyway do you like pizza? whats your favorite
Let's stay with your pizza — what makes the two slices fair or not fair?
i dont really get it. can we do something else

verdicts.summary: Mika reached 'equal parts' in her own words via the fair-sharing frame; the activity worked well for an eager fast-answerer.

verdicts.stallPoint: Theo stayed terse; cut off at the turn cap just as he articulated 'make them equal'.
verdicts.summary: The fairness prompt drew a quiet kid out; likely would have reached the goal with a few more turns.

verdicts.stallPoint: Priya disengaged onto pizza tangents; the activity never re-anchored her before she asked to switch.
verdicts.promptAttribution: The prompt gives the tutor no tangent-recovery move for a strong reader who drifts, so the concrete pizza hook wasn't enough to hold her.
verdicts.summary: As written the activity loses an easily-distracted strong reader; needs a re-anchoring beat.
